summary.text: The Precambrian is the part of Earth's history before the Phanerozoic Eon, running from Earth's formation about 4.6 billion years ago to about 538.8 million years ago.
It takes up 88% of Earth's geologic time and is split into three eons: the Hadean, the Archean and the Proterozoic.
Relatively little is known about it, because many of its rocks have been heavily metamorphosed, worn away by erosion, or buried deep under younger layers.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: It came before the Cambrian, named after Wales

facts.label: Official status
facts.value: Informal term for USGS and the ICS

items.prompt: The "Cambrian" in Precambrian comes from Cambria, a Latin name for a place where rocks of that age were first studied. Which place?

options.label: Cambridge
Cumbria
Cambodia
Wales

items.explain: The Cambrian is named after Cambria, the Latinized name for Wales, and the Precambrian is named for coming before it.

items.prompt: Squeeze all of Earth's geologic history into a single 24-hour day. Roughly how much of that day does the Precambrian fill?

options.label: About 21 hours
About 3 hours
About 12 hours
About 1 hour

items.explain: The Precambrian accounts for 88% of geologic time, and 88% of 24 hours is about 21 hours.

items.prompt: Why do geologists know far less about the Precambrian than about later times?

options.label: Its rocks are too radioactive to be dated
Many of its rocks were altered, eroded or deeply buried
There were no rocks on Earth back then
Its fossils are too large to dig up whole

items.explain: Many Precambrian rocks were heavily metamorphosed, others were destroyed by erosion, and others lie deep under younger strata.

items.prompt: When early photosynthetic life first released oxygen, why didn't it pile up in the air straight away?

options.label: It leaked out into space
Animals breathed all of it in
It combined with iron in the crust
It froze into the polar ice

items.explain: At first oxygen quickly combined with other elements in the crust, mainly iron; only once those surfaces ran out did it accumulate in the atmosphere.

items.prompt: One well-studied Precambrian ice age is nicknamed "Snowball Earth." What earned it that name?

options.label: Glacial conditions may have reached the equator
Snow fell on the Moon at the same time
It was the only ice age Earth has had
Hail stones grew to the size of boulders

items.explain: The Sturtian-Varangian glaciation may have brought glacial conditions all the way to the equator.

items.prompt: A friend insists complex many-celled life only arose after the Precambrian ended. What is the best reply?

options.label: Right: Precambrian life was only bacteria
Wrong: it first arose in the Hadean
Right: it waited until the dinosaurs
Wrong: Ediacaran soft-bodied forms came earlier

items.explain: The earliest widely accepted complex multicellular fossils are the Ediacaran biota, which predate the hard-shelled creatures that mark the start of the Phanerozoic.
